title: Talent ramp check-in: new hires & interview debriefs (Mar 4, 2025)
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick internal sync covering: - this week’s interview debrief highlights, - onboarding sensor checks for hires in the last 6 weeks, - buddy rotation adjustments, and - follow-ups for hiring pipeline. Aim: identify blockers to new-hire productivity and short-cycle fixes we can apply this sprint.

Summary (TL;DR):
- 3 candidate debriefs this week: one strong backend infra hire (offer extended), one needs second system design loop, one rejected for culture/communication mismatch.
- Onboarding pulse: 5 active new hires (1wk, 2wk, 3wk, 5wk, 6wk). Two ramp metrics off-target: time-to-first-PR and infra access delays.
- Quick wins agreed: streamline infra access ticket, schedule shadowing sessions for 1st-weekers, update buddy checklist to include quick greeter doc.

Interview debriefs (notes):
1) Candidate A — Backend/Serving (onsite loop 2025-03-03)
- Strengths: system thinking, latency-focused anecdotes, explained KV cache tradeoffs clearly.
- Risks: limited Rust experience (we're using Rust in some runtime pieces), but strong C++/Go background.
- Interviewer consensus: strong hire if compensation aligns.
- Outcome: Offer extended (recruiter following up).
- Action: Arjun to draft counter-offer + note on training plan for Rust ramp. (Due: 2025-03-07)

2) Candidate B — Infra/SRE (loop 2025-03-02)
- Strengths: on-call experience at scale, good incident war stories.
- Gaps: struggled on distributed locking design Q; needs deeper distributed systems fundamentals for our autoscaling code paths.
- Interviewer ask: bring candidate back for a focused DS question set (1 hour).
- Outcome: Hold and re-run targeted interview.
- Action: Leah to assemble 30-min targeted assessment and run on 2025-03-10.

3) Candidate C — Platform PM (panel 2025-03-01)
- Feedback: good roadmap instincts but communication style flagged by two interviewers as too directive for current team culture.
- Outcome: decline; recruiter to send gracious rejection and feedback.

Onboarding pulse (new hires):
- New hire roster:
  * N1 (Software Engineer) — start 2025-02-24 — week 1
  * N2 (Infra Engineer) — start 2025-02-17 — week 2
  * N3 (Platform Eng) — start 2025-02-10 — week 3
  * N4 (SRE) — start 2025-01-20 — week 5
  * N5 (DevEx Intern) — start 2024-12-15 — week 6

Pulse metrics (rough):
- Time to first PR (goal <= 7 days): N1 = 9d, N2 = 6d, N3 = 12d, N4 = 8d, N5 = 3d.
- Infra access SLA (goal <= 48h): N1 waited 72h for GPU lab access (blocked on ticket), N3 waited 96h for K8s namespace; N2 and others within SLA.
- Buddy touchpoints (goal 3x/week first 2 weeks): N1 reported 2x, N2 reported 4x, N3 reported 1x.

Observations / root causes:
- Infra access delays mostly due to manual handoffs between infra-oncall and security approval for KMS keys. Ticket annotations unclear.
- Onboarding checklist missing an explicit "first-day greeter" step; new hires sometimes unsure where to go for immediate help (Slack channel vs. email).
- Time-to-first-PR variance correlates with repo complexity and whether a starter ticket is provided; N3 was given a larger-scope task without a small starter task.

Buddy system notes:
- Current rotation: 1 primary buddy + 1 secondary for first 2 months.
- Pain point: buddies overloaded with review requests; some buddy expectations not documented.
- Proposed change: add a "starter-pr template" that buddy or team lead attaches to a new hire’s first ticket and a weekly 30-min sync in week 1.
- Action: Priya to draft starter-pr template + short buddy checklist. (Due: 2025-03-11)

Concrete action items (owners + due dates):
- Streamline infra access flow: create a labelled playbook for infra access requests, include escalation contacts and KMS approval steps. Owner: Tomás. Due: 2025-03-12.
- Rework first-ticket policy: ensure every new hire gets a <4h starter task. Owner: Leah. Due: 2025-03-09.
- Buddy checklist + starter-PR template. Owner: Priya. Due: 2025-03-11.
- Run targeted DS interview for Candidate B. Owner: Leah. Date: 2025-03-10.
- Offer follow-up and Rust ramp plan for Candidate A. Owner: Arjun. Due: 2025-03-07.
- Postmortem note on onboarding delays for Q1 hires (doc + proposals). Owner: Maya. Due: 2025-03-20.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we want to make buddy weekly syncs mandatory in the first month, or keep recommended? (ops cost vs improved ramp)
- Should we invest engineering hours this quarter to automate infra access approvals (low-touch flow) or continue manual fixes and monitor?
- Do we create a "starter ticket" archetype in Jira templates? (if yes, need ticket form changes)

Requests for leadership / asks:
- Requesting 4 hours of infra-engineering capacity this sprint to prototype the access automation (or at minimum, reduce manual steps). Please advise.
- Support from hiring committee to fast-track offer approvals when comp benchmarking takes longer than 48h. We lost a candidate last quarter to delay.

Meeting log / standup snippets (this week):
- 2025-03-03 10:00AM — Onboarding sync: N1 flagged GPU access; we opened a ticket and included infra-oncall. Action: Tomás to follow up.
- 2025-03-03 3:00PM — Interviewers debrief: Candidate A recommended for hire; compensation discussion.
- 2025-03-04 9:30AM — Buddy rotation planning: adjusted schedule to reduce overlap for mentors with heavy reviews.

Notes-to-self / informal: 
- We should capture micro-feedback from every new hire at day 3 (very short pulse) — quick form + one-line NPS-ish question. Could wire this into Slack via a bot.
- Consider pairing new hires with short "whiteboard sessions" in week 1 to surface knowledge gaps early.

Appendix (links & references):
- Onboarding playbook (v2): confluence://onboarding/playbook-v2
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-4521 (starter ticket policy)
- Slack threads: #onboard-ops, #hiring-review (see thread timestamp 2025-03-03 15:12)

Next check-in: 2025-03-11 (weekly cadence)

End of notes.
